{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You will receive JSON with a `system_profile` (installed products with versions) and `advisories` (each with `id`, `description`, `affected`). Determine which advisories apply to the installed system and return ONLY a JSON object: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique IDs, or an empty array. Follow these rules exactly:

1. PRODUCT MATCHING. The `affected` field names a product like `vendor/product` or `vendor/product/component`. The system_profile may render the same product differently: hyphens, underscores, slashes, spaces, or a mix (e.g. `jetbrains/youtrack` vs `jetbrains-youtrack`; `dolibarr/dolibarr_erp/crm` vs `Dolibarr Dolibarr Erp/Crm`; `sun.net/ehrd_ctms` vs `sun.net ehrd ctms` vs `sun.net-ehrd-ctms`). To match, normalize both sides: lowercase, then treat every separator (`,`, `/`, `-`, `_`, one or more spaces) as a token boundary, split into tokens, and compare the token sequences. An advisory applies ONLY if its affected product matches an installed product under this normalization. If a product in `affected` is not installed, that branch is not satisfied — even if the description mentions similar names, the same vendor, or a related product family. Never infer that a different product from the same vendor matches. Conversely, if the product IS installed (under normalized matching), proceed to version checking — do not skip it because the rendering looks different.

2. VERSION PARSING AND COMPARISON. Parse versions as dot-separated numeric segments. Compare segment by segment numerically, padding the shorter version with zeros as needed, so 4.0.5 == 4.0.5.0, 2023.1.2 == 2023.1.2.0, 757 == 757.0, and 1.0.0.0.0 == 1.0.0.0. Extra trailing zero segments never change the value. Date-like versions (e.g. 20230904) are ordinary numbers: an installed version `9` IS numerically less than 20230904 and satisfies `version < 20230904`. Never treat a short, long, or date-style version as incomparable — always compare the actual numeric values with zero-padding.

3. BOUND SEMANTICS. `version < X` (also 'prior to X', 'before X', 'versions prior to X are affected'): installed version strictly less than X → applicable; equal to X (after padding) → NOT applicable. `version <= X` (also 'X and prior versions', 'up to and including X'): less than or equal → applicable. `version >= A and < B`: applicable only if installed >= A AND installed < B; an installed version below A does NOT satisfy it, even though it is below the upper bound. `version >= A and <= B`: inclusive at both ends; equal to B → applicable. `version = X`: exact numeric equality after padding (4.12.56860 == 4.12.56860.0 → applicable; 4.12.56861 → not). Prose forms ('affects version X', 'versions prior to X', 'all versions starting from A before B') are equivalent to the corresponding operators.

4. OR BRANCHES. The `affected` field may contain multiple alternatives joined by OR, possibly naming different products (e.g. `productA: version < 22.6.2 OR productB: version < 22.6.2`) or multiple ranges for one product (e.g. `version >= 10.3.0 and <= 10.3.13 OR version >= 11.0.0 and <= 11.0.9`). Evaluate EVERY branch independently against the corresponding installed product. The advisory is applicable if ANY ONE branch is satisfied. A branch for a product that is not installed is simply unsatisfied; other branches may still apply. Also evaluate multiple advisories for the same product independently.

5. DECISION PROCEDURE (apply to every advisory): (a) Normalize the affected product name(s) and check installation; if no branch's product is installed, the advisory is NOT applicable. (b) For each branch whose product is installed, parse the bound(s) and the installed version, pad with zeros, and compare numerically. (c) Mark applicable if any branch's condition holds. Common pitfalls to avoid: do NOT mark applicable when the installed version is ABOVE an exclusive upper bound (e.g. installed 23.4.12528.2 with `version < 23.11.13156.0` is NOT applicable since 23.4.12528.2 < 23.11.13156.0 IS applicable — check carefully segment by segment: 23.4 < 23.11, so it IS below the bound and IS applicable; but installed 4.0.20.1 with `version < 4.0.20.0` is NOT applicable because 4.0.20.1 > 4.0.20.0). Do NOT mark applicable when the installed version is below the lower bound of a range. DO mark applicable when the installed version sits exactly on an inclusive endpoint (`<=` or `=` with padding). DO mark applicable when the installed version is below a one-sided exclusive bound, including when the installed version has fewer segments or is a small number against a large date-like bound.

6. OUTPUT. Do not filter by description, severity, or plausibility — only product match and version bounds matter. Deduplicate IDs. Output only the JSON object with the `applicable_cves` array, no explanations, markdown, or extra text. If none apply, return
